prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1192; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact collision at an intersection. Claimant reports a shoulder injury and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is named on it. Coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the impact and describes damage consistent with a side impact.

Entry 4: Statements from two independent witnesses and the other driver all match the claimant's description of how the collision occurred.

Entry 5: Photographs of the vehicle show damage that lines up well with the reported impact point and direction of force.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant's attorney to confirm the medical authorization forms and request the initial treatment records.

Entry 7: Reviewed the vehicle's prior repair history and found no earlier damage to the areas affected in this collision.

Entry 8: Medical records show a shoulder injury that fits the kind and force of a side impact. No prior treatment to the same body area appears in the records we have obtained.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of shoulder injury. Requested updated treatment notes to understand the recovery timeline.

Entry 10: Claimant has given the same account of the accident in each conversation, including the recorded statement and the follow-up call with counsel present.

Entry 11: Reviewed the file with no concerns about the timing of the damage or the coverage period. Claim remains open pending the updated treatment notes and the attorney's demand package.
